messages:
sophia: FYI seeing intermittent packet loss on overlay during large GPU backfills in us-west-2. RDMA jobs erroring out with retransmits and some grpc timeouts. anyone else?
netbot: alert: vxlan_encap_drops on gpu-node-12 jumped to 420 in 5m (metric: net.encap.drops).
dave: which interface? vxlan0? can you paste `ip -s link show vxlan0` and a tcpdump?
li: tcpdump from gpu-node-12 while repro: `tcpdump -n -i vxlan0 udp and port 4789 -c 200` shows lots of retransmit pairs. ip stats: RX: 120000 packets, 1100 errors, 720 dropped.
marcos: any recent kernel or mlx5 driver changes on that fleet? we pushed a host kernel bump last week to 5.15.78 -> 5.15.110 on a subset.
sophia: correct, nodes in the backfill pool were upgraded last Thurs. not all hosts. failing hosts are 5.15.110 and have mlx5 driver from vendor 5.0.1.
dave: logs look like coalesced fragments being dropped. RDMA + VXLAN + large frames frequently hit MTU boundaries. can you run `ethtool -k <physdev>` and `cat /sys/class/net/<physdev>/mtu` on affected hosts?
li: quick dump: `ethtool -k eth0` shows GRO: on, GSO: on, LRO: off. MTU is 9000 on phys nic, vxlan0 MTU 1450 (we downsize to avoid underlay).
marcos: aha — vxlan MTU mismatch + offloads enabled on phys nic + driver regression in mlx5 -> kernel coalescing creates oversized skbs, kernel drops when encap pushes size > underlying path MTU.
jen: can we mitigate without rolling back kernel? maybe disable GRO/GSO on the vxlan interface as a canary. tradeoff: CPU up but less drops.
sophia: trying that on two hosts now: `ethtool -K vxlan0 gro off gso off`
jen: any change?
sophia: within 2 mins drop counters fell from ~400/min to single digits. RDMA jobs that were failing recovered.
dave: nice. let's patch a small playbook: disable GRO on vxlan for affected hosts and throttle backfill batch size while we plan driver bump.
infra-oncall: rolling apply to 12 hosts in us-west-2 backfill pool. will schedule driver upgrade to vendor mlx5 5.1.0 in next maintenance window. created ticket INF-6421.
marcos: long term we should align vxlan MTU with phys MTU or enable proper PMP/DF handling so encap doesn't overflow. also open a vendor SR for mlx5 coalescing regression.
li: note: customers with RDMA-sensitive workloads (training jobs) saw the most impact. we should add a node label to avoid cross-AZ scheduling for backfills until fixed.
jen: adding a temporary scheduler constraint `node.kubernetes.io/rdma-safe=yes` and a small autoscaler tweak to prefer same-AZ placements for large backfills.
sophia: summary: root cause appears to be kernel/driver coalescing + MTU mismatch causing encap oversize and drops. temp fix: ethtool -K vxlan0 gro off gso off on affected hosts + reduce batch sizes + schedule driver bump.
marcos: will follow up with vendor SR and a postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:
